title: Learning to read and piano influences
summary: He learned to read on jitney jobs, was taught chords by David John, and admired house-party pianists like Lil Willie.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: No I wasn't. I learned how to read after I went to play on a Jitney job. Oh I see. I used to buy so much music I just had to learn something. I had fellows in the band to help me and sing along until I learned as much as I did now.
Did you have a teacher on piano at all? Or did you pick it up?
No I didn't have a teacher on piano but the fellow by the name of David John used to teach me when I was working around with him. He used to teach me chords, how to form them and invade them.
Did you have any particular piano player that you used to listen to a lot?

Well I used to like to listen to Clarence Gabriel, Lil Willie, Fat Bichon. Which Lil Willie is that? There was a piano player by the name of Lil Willie. He was a house party piano player. He could play the piano.
Did you see the guy that got killed a couple of Mardi Gras ago? I think it was?
No I think he died a natural death. Willie Forrest, huh?
No, not him. Not Willie Forrest?

We used to call him Long-Head Willie. Yeah, Lil Long-Head. He used to play all them house parties. Him, Red Caillou, Udell, Walter Pelliborn. They used to have regular jam sessions like bands they have now on the piano. I was quite a youngster. I used to go around and listen to them. Try to imitate them. Go home and start playing. Try to get what they get on the piano.
Do you still play piano or something?

Well I know the instrument. I'll sit down sometimes and make a few chords but hardly I don't worry with it too much because I don't have it at home. You see if I had one at home probably you know what I mean. I would play at nine then on the job I'd make a few chords.
I have seen you play piano on Burbank Street. I forget who was in the band. Myrtle Jones was singing.
That's right. That's right. The boy didn't know her number and he couldn't play her music so I had to you know fill in.
